98: They taught - that [land] can be acquired by means of money alone only in a place where it is not customary to write a bill of sale.

One does not acquire - since it is customary [to write documents], the buyer does not rely [on the sale being valid] until he takes the document; his primary intention is to acquire by means of the document.
And if he specified - whether my intention is that my money effects the acquisition or my document effects the acquisition.
